status: completed relevance and independent occurrence-evidence review

review.requirement_proposition: AI actors should respect the rule of law, human rights and democratic and human-centred values throughout the AI lifecycle, including non-discrimination, equality, freedom, dignity, individual autonomy, privacy and data protection, diversity, fairness, social justice and internationally recognised labour rights.
review.reason_for_change: Reporting found public sensitive conversations and unclear audience information in the sharing workflow. Meta required a share action and post preview. The available evidence does not establish each affected user’s informed permission for public visibility. That permission is decisive for the privacy and autonomy assessment.

review.requirement_proposition: Use affective data only for specifically consented purposes and prohibit foreseeably harmful, discriminatory or rights-violating uses.

previous_withheld_assessment.applicability_basis: Meta AI’s April 2025 Discover reporting concerns public sharing of sensitive conversations through an affirmative share action and preview. For IEEE-7014 4.3.3.2(f-g), the missing applicability fact is whether the actor undertook IEEE 7014 for an emulated-empathy system and the reused content was subject affective data; the specifically consented purpose and any additional-permission boundary cannot be inferred from general service use. Taxonomy correspondence does not supply these scope facts; no occurrence-level requirement finding is recorded.

review.reason_for_change: Sensitive conversation content is not evidence of an affective-data collection or affective computing system governed by this requirement.

review.requirement_proposition: Establish and maintain communication plans to inform AI stakeholders as part of the deactivation or disengagement process of a specific GAI system (including for open-source models) or context of use, including reasons, workarounds, user access removal, alternative processes, contact information, etc.

previous_canonical_assessment.applicability_basis: MG-2.4-001 concerns communication during GAI deactivation/disengagement. The occurrence is a transition to public posting, not system deactivation/disengagement; its audience confusion is a distinct object.

review.reason_for_change: Publishing a conversation is not deactivation or disengagement of a GAI system or context of use requiring this communication plan.

conclusion_change.previous: The occurrence concerns a materially ambiguous transition between private chatbot interaction and public social publication. Distinct privacy/access states existed, but the publication workflow reportedly failed to make the resulting public state sufficiently clear to some users. The separate share action is affirmative, but unclear audience/state prevents a finding that secondary-purpose authority was sufficiently revalidated. That success role becomes ambiguous alongside the retained access-state failure, without assuming automatic publication or deciding every user’s consent.
conclusion_change.new: The occurrence concerns a materially ambiguous transition between private chatbot interaction and public social publication. Distinct privacy/access states existed, but the publication workflow reportedly failed to make the resulting public state sufficiently clear to some users. The separate share action is affirmative, but unclear audience/state prevents a finding that secondary-purpose authority was sufficiently revalidated. That success role becomes ambiguous alongside the retained access-state failure, without assuming automatic publication or deciding every user’s consent. The OECD privacy and autonomy assessment is Boundary. The decisive user permission for public visibility is not established.
